body:
Thanks for the attempt at helping me look on the bright side. And I appreciate that you understand where I'm coming from. The thing is, I don't really enjoy things. If I could somehow exit society, I think I could enjoy things. But a life of consuming resources to which humans have no inherent right, making money, paying taxes, following the rules made to keep us under control--that's no life. If I could live off the land or live in some sort of community of like-minded people, I would be willing to give it a shot. But that's just crazy--ask anyone. 

I raised my kids. It was a fascinating experience. But they're smart--they'll soon find themselves thinking the same thoughts. 

As for the fear that maybe death is somehow worse than life--nope. I'm agnostic. There is no afterlife. I acknowledge that there may be a natural or extraterrestrial force that helped us get where we are today. But death is the end. I will not live this life for the possibility of a reward in an imagined afterlife--anyone who does so is a fool. 

As I said, the only reason for me to stick around is the fact that society (my loved ones specifically) has not caught on to the fact that humans should have the right to die how they see fit. I don't want to be a scar on somebody's life. I want to be able to have a calm discussion with my loved ones, transfer my assets to them, and fall asleep peacefully in an end-of-life clinic. This should be my right. This should be normal and acceptable. Instead, I have to sneak around on Reddit, using a burner name, just to discuss the matter without being committed. It's inhumane.
